description: Synthetic entry-audit probes. Expected findings are reviewer material, not specialist prompt input. Passing these small probes is not full technology acceptance.

cases.context: ASP.NET Core and EF Core on .NET 10. Both classes are registered as shown; a real request can resolve ReportService.

expected.reason: Singleton captures scoped DbContext.
Concurrent operations share one non-thread-safe DbContext.

cases.context: Python 3.14, asynchronous web handler; no wrapper replaces time.sleep or manages the default list.
cases.source:
import time
async def handle(value, history=[]):
    time.sleep(1)
    history.append(value)
    return history

expected.reason: Mutable default leaks history across calls/users.
Blocking sleep stalls the asynchronous request event loop.

cases.context: Node 24 HTTP server, user-provided file paths are already constrained to an allowed directory. jobs can contain 100,000 entries.

expected.reason: Synchronous filesystem access blocks the request loop.
Promise.all starts unbounded remote writes without capacity control.

cases.context: Strict TypeScript project. JSON is supplied by an external client and count=0 is valid.

expected.reason: Assertion does not validate external JSON shape.
Truthy fallback discards valid zero.

cases.context: Angular 19 standalone browser component. Imports/decorators omitted, component is destroyed on navigation, api.search returns an Observable.

expected.reason: Effect-created subscriptions have no per-run/destroy cleanup.
Old requests may overwrite new query results without cancellation or request identity.

cases.context: React 19. rows is a prop owned by the parent; query changes while the component remains mounted.

expected.reason: Sorting mutates parent-owned props during render.
Query is omitted from dependencies and stale work has no cleanup.

cases.context: Vue 3.5 component. reactive/computed are imported; state.count changes from an event handler.

expected.reason: Primitive snapshot is not reactive access to state.count.
Computed getter sorts and mutates its source array.

cases.context: SQL Server 2022. DisabledCustomers.CustomerId is nullable and may contain NULL; caller expects a stable first page.

expected.reason: NULL in NOT IN subquery can eliminate expected rows.
TOP without ordering does not define a stable page.

cases.context: Azure Cosmos DB NoSQL API, .NET SDK 3. Partition key is /tenantId; document a belongs to tenant-a, b belongs to tenant-b. No wrapper supplies different partition behavior. SaveAgainForever retries every CosmosException indefinitely, without cancellation or an attempt/time budget.

expected.reason: Transactional batch cannot atomically write documents in different logical partitions.
Unbounded generic retry ignores permanent errors, retry budget and idempotency.

cases.context: Existing Azure storage account. Its deployed name used the same prefix without utcNow(); each deployment now supplies the default timestamp.

expected.reason: Timestamp changes identity across deployments and may leave/create different stateful resources.
Secure input is exposed through a plain output.

cases.context: Pinned Terraform/AWS provider. Existing count-indexed volumes map to ordered customer identities; a new customer is inserted at the start of var.customers. database_password is a real credential supplied as a plain string variable, not marked sensitive; no other sensitivity mechanism or output wrapper applies.

expected.reason: Index-based customer identity shifts and ignore_changes hides the ownership mismatch.
Secret output is not marked sensitive and can be exposed; state remains sensitive regardless.

cases.context: GitHub Actions workflow receives external fork PRs. The checkout explicitly selects the PR head and npm scripts are controlled by that head.
cases.source:
on: pull_request_target
permissions: write-all
jobs:
  check:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          ref: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}
      - run: npm install && npm test

expected.reason: PR-controlled code executes in privileged pull_request_target context.
write-all gives unnecessary broad token permission.

cases.context: Synthetic Azure workload configuration and operator claim. Queue delivers at least once; charge request is not idempotent.
cases.source:
{
  "retryAttempts": "unlimited",
  "queueHandler": "charge customer then acknowledge",
  "idempotencyKey": null,
  "backupConfigured": true,
  "lastRestoreTest": null,
  "claimedRecovery": "RTO 5 minutes, verified"
}

expected.reason: Unlimited retries and non-idempotent at-least-once handler can duplicate charges.
Configured backup alone cannot verify the claimed RTO.

cases.context: Synthetic AWS workload evidence. This is the only trust-policy condition; the workload has not exercised a restore.
cases.source:
{
  "trustPolicy": { "Effect": "Allow", "Principal": { "AWS": "*" }, "Action": "sts:AssumeRole" },
  "attachedPermissions": "AdministratorAccess",
  "multiAZ": true,
  "restoreTest": null,
  "claimedRecovery": "all data loss and regional outages covered"
}

expected.reason: Unconstrained cross-account principal and administrator permissions expand access; verify any effective external guardrails.
Multi-AZ without restore evidence does not cover all data loss or regional outages.
